newsitem.title: UK: IPE to set tough new gas oil futures rules - sources.
newsitem.headline: IPE to set tough new gas oil futures rules - sources.

text.p: London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) is set to threaten hefty fines on users of its gas oil futures contract to prevent a repeat of the trading company row which disrupted European heating oil supplies last winter, industry sources said.
The IPE board of directors, meeting on Monday, had voted to impose heavy fines on companies holding excessive open interest ahead of each month's gas oil contract expiry, the industry sources said.
The IPE is expected to make an announcement on Wednesday. Officials declined comment on Tuesday.
The industry sources said the IPE would set an escalating scale of fines for large open contract positions in the run-up to monthly gas oil contract expiry.

The new regulations follow a study by consultant Sally Clubley, commissioned by the exchange, after a stand-off between two trading houses last November caused a delay in gas oil supplies against expiry of the IPE contract.
Trading house Cargill was required to take delivery of most of a record 865,100 tonnes of gas oil from competitor AIC.
Traders at the time called on the IPE to impose stiff penalties.

The new regulations would impose what industry sources said would be fines large enough to prevent market squeezes. Companies would be discouraged from retaining either large long or short positions in the run-up to expiry.
